newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - SOUTH AFRICA - SEPT 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - SOUTH AFRICA - SEPT 17.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Tuesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Former state president PW Botha, former law and order minister Louis le Grange and seven police generals had approved a host of raids into neighbouring countries in the 1980s which left at least 18 people dead, convicted government assassin Eugene de Kock said.
- The finance department was working on phasing out special bond deals with institutional investors which allowed them to bypass money and capital markets, market sources said.
- Oil and petrochemical producer Sasol lifted attributable earnings 25.5 percent to 2.33 billion rand in the year to June.
- Parliament's public service committee voted unanimously to give public servants the right to retire from the age of 55.

- Health Minister Nkosazana Zuma came under fire when new regulations which will stop most doctors dispensing medicine were sharply criticised by doctors' associations, community organisations and some clergy.
- SANCO Investment Holdings has purchased a 10 percent stake in SMG Holdings for 24.9 million rand from controlling shareholder Redbridge Assets.
- Consolidated Frame Textiles Ltd , South Africa's largest textile compay, is in talks to take control of Romatex Ltd , said Confram chief executive Roy Sable.
- Sasol, the chemical and fuel-from-coal producer, lifted earnings per share 21.7 percent to 393.1 cents for the year to June.
- Sun International will dismiss at least 4,000 employees locked out of its resorts last week, if they fail to accept the hotel group's final wage offer, the company said.
- Old Mutual, the country's largest insurer ranked by assets, said group income in the year to June 30 rose 12 percent.

- Eugene de Kock, the convicted police hit-squad killer, named senior government officials, police and military officers who ordered him and his counter-insurgency unit to kill and maim people in Swaziland, Lesotho and South Africa.
